resolutionVerdicts.reason: Branch's package.json owns the whole dependency-tree shape and main's diff for this file really is the single @playwright/test line (confirmed under pw-001); taking the branch as base and bumping only that line is correct.

Regenerating under the pinned npm rather than hand-merging is the right call given the tree divergence, and `packageManager: "npm@11.6.2"` is indeed present on the branch today (restored by commit f9c9bce after s20-tooling-convergence had deleted it — see lockfileFinding).
resolutionVerdicts.correction: The resolution's phrasing ('run `npm install`') understates the mechanism. s20's ins commit (1d3869c) deleted the `install:pinned-npm` npm script, and the later f9c9bce follow-up restored only the `packageManager` field and `scripts/npm-version.js`, NOT `install:pinned-npm`. A plain `npm install` on this branch today uses whatever npm is ambient on PATH (11.17.0 in this workspace per s10's own baseline), not 11.6.2, unless corepack is enabled and configured to honour `packageManager` automatically. The safe, already-proven-in-this-repo-family command is `npx --yes "$(node scripts/npm-version.js)" install`, then `npm ci` to prove it installs clean under 11.6.2 (see lockfileFinding).

resolutionVerdicts.reason: Re-ran `git merge-tree` myself (see pw-004): zero conflict markers for either file. `npm ci` as a post-merge sanity check is sound and cheap.

Same clean-merge proof as animals holds for plants (see pw-004). The `npm ci` sanity check is not merely optional belt-and-braces here: plants' own main history for this exact bump (commit ecccaad, then a same-day follow-up 7b121f9 titled 'fix: regenerate package-lock.json with pinned npm version', changing a further 443 lines) is a live example of `npm ci` failing in CI because a lockfile for this identical one-line playwright bump was first regenerated under the wrong local npm. The sanity check is load-bearing, not precautionary.

Confirmed via `git log <mergeBase>..origin/feat/NO_JIRA-frontend-alignment -- <path>` for all four paths: no commits. Nothing of the branch's to preserve; taking main's content verbatim via the merge is correct.

verdictHolds.reason: The 'port' verdict and its repo-by-repo split (ins needs manual work + a lockfile regen; animals/plants/tests are clean) is correct and independently reproduced. Two caveats worth flagging: (1) the top-level `summary` sentence overstates scope — it says the playwright bump is 'the ONLY package.json change main made in this window in each repo' for 'all four repos', but tests' package.json actually changed TWO lines (`@playwright/cli` 0.1.14->0.1.21 in addition to `@playwright/test`), which the survey's own `behaviourChanges` and `files` sections correctly capture elsewhere — only the summary sentence is loose. (2) the ins lockfile-regen resolution names the wrong mechanism post-s20 (see resolutionVerdicts and lockfileFinding) — the intent (npm 11.6.2) is right, the literal command ('npm install') is not sufficient on its own.

lockfileFinding.handoverClaim: An older handover said ins and the tests repo install with plain npm, with only animals and plants pinned to npm 11.6.2 via packageManager.
lockfileFinding.verdict: The old handover is stale for ins, accurate as-is for the other three. ins's branch DID lose the pin: s20-tooling-convergence (commit 1d3869c4, 16 Sept) deleted `packageManager`, `scripts/npm-version.js` and `install:pinned-npm` from all three frontends as part of Sam's ruling 17/18 ("the npm pin goes; the lockfiles get fixed instead"). But 36 minutes later, commit f9c9bce ('keep npm-version.js for main's workflow_run jobs') re-added `packageManager` and `scripts/npm-version.js` to ins ONLY, because ins main's lighthouse-equivalent workflow_run jobs still read that field and call that script against whatever code is checked out, including this branch's. Reading origin/feat/NO_JIRA-frontend-alignment today confirms ins is pinned again. animals and plants never lost the pin (main has always had `packageManager: "npm@11.6.2"`, so nothing there needed restoring). tests has never had a packageManager field, on either main or the branch, and remains genuinely plain-npm today, exactly as the old handover said.

lockfileRegenerationCommands.ins: After resolving the package.json conflict (branch as base, bump the @playwright/test line to 1.63.0), do NOT run a bare `npm install`/`npm ci` — `install:pinned-npm` no longer exists as an npm script (deleted in s20, never restored). Run `npx --yes "$(node scripts/npm-version.js)" install` to regenerate package-lock.json under the pinned npm 11.6.2, then `npm ci` to prove it installs clean.
lockfileRegenerationCommands.animals: No regen strictly required (trial-merge is clean). As a sanity check run `npm ci` — `packageManager: "npm@11.6.2"` is present on both main and branch, so corepack/CI already resolve the right npm; a bare `npm ci` on a machine with corepack enabled is safe here.
lockfileRegenerationCommands.plants: Same as animals, but treat the `npm ci` check as load-bearing rather than optional: plants' own main history (commits ecccaad then 7b121f9) shows this exact playwright bump broke `npm ci` in CI the first time because the lockfile was regenerated under the wrong local npm, and needed a second full regen under 11.6.2 to fix. Do not skip the check on the assumption a one-line bump can't do this.
lockfileRegenerationCommands.tests: No regen required and no npm pin to honour — merge takes main's already-CI-proven package.json/package-lock.json/Dockerfile/bin script verbatim (branch never touched any of them). tests' own CI npm comes from `node-version-file`/`.nvmrc` via actions/setup-node, unaffected by this cluster.
